claim: The academic-benchmark era was defined by MMLU (57 subjects, multiple-choice), BIG-bench, Stanford HELM (holistic axes), and EleutherAI lm-eval-harness, with successor chains like GLUE to SuperGLUE and MMLU to MMLU-Pro.
quote: MMLU... is a benchmark for evaluating LLMs... covering 57 subjects... MMLU-Pro... increased the number of answer choices to make problems more challenging

claim: OpenAI released Evals as an open-source framework alongside GPT-4 in March 2023, aiming to crowdsource benchmarks and granting GPT-4 access to high-quality contributors.
quote: OpenAI hopes to crowdsource AI model testing... OpenAI planned to grant GPT-4 access to those who contribute high-quality benchmarks

claim: By 2026 static benchmarks have a median discriminative lifespan under two years; HumanEval and GPQA Diamond are saturated (frontier models >94%, vs 65% for PhD experts), and SWE-bench Verified gold patches can be reproduced verbatim from task IDs.
quote: Median discriminative lifespan under two years before ceiling effects erode ranking signal... reproduce the original gold patch or problem statements from the eval verbatim with minimal prompting, using just the task ID

claim: Agent evaluation in 2025-2026 centers on GAIA, SWE-bench Verified, OSWorld, Tau2-bench (pass^k reliability metric), and WebArena, but suffers a standardization gap where even 'success' is encoded incompatibly across SWE-bench, AppWorld, and Tau-bench.
quote: A simple notion like success appears as a Boolean resolved flag in SWE-bench, a success field in AppWorld, and an implicit reward of 1 in Tau-bench... underscore the need for consolidation and standardization

claim: The 2024-2026 eval-platform layer (Confident AI/DeepEval, Braintrust, Galileo, W&B Weave, Ragas) shifted from static leaderboards toward domain-specific custom metrics covering RAG, agents, chatbots, multi-turn, and safety with 50+ research-backed metrics.
quote: Covers every eval use case (RAG, agents, chatbots, single-turn, multi-turn, safety) with 50+ research-backed metrics... production-to-eval pipelines, and CI/CD regression testing

claim: Evals are now table stakes for shipping LLM products because AI apps fail differently from deterministic software: a PR can pass every unit test while the model silently gets worse, so teams gate deploys on offline gold-set evals plus online production evals.
quote: A pull request can pass every unit test, type check, and uptime check while the AI becomes worse at the task

claim: The LLM observability/eval platform market is sized at $1.97B in 2025 growing to $2.69B in 2026 (36.3% CAGR), driven by production monitoring needs and rising hallucination and safety concerns.
quote: The LLM observability platform market will grow from $1.97 billion in 2025 to $2.69 billion in 2026 at a CAGR of 36.3%

claim: The three structural failure modes of static benchmarks are saturation (top models cluster near ceiling), contamination (test data leaks into training), and gameability (optimizing to the benchmark without real-world gains).
quote: The three core problems are saturation, contamination, and gameability
